Note::TexAccessor::simplify_fractions¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::simplify_fractions() const

Canonicalize Fraction Source Without Rendering It¶

simplify_fractions() rewrites complete \frac, \dfrac, \tfrac, and \cfrac calls to one canonical \frac{numerator}{denominator} spelling. Use it when TeX must remain TeX but display-style variants and incidental outer whitespace should no longer affect comparison or downstream processing. Use frac_slash() when the desired result is arithmetic text such as (a)/(b), and canonicalize_macros() when several unrelated legacy control words should be normalized together.

Matching is lexical, exact, and case-sensitive. Both required arguments must be balanced braced groups. Nested braces and nested fraction calls are supported; recognized fractions inside either argument are normalized recursively. Only ASCII whitespace at each argument’s outer edge is removed. Content inside the argument, unrelated commands, escaped linebreak-like spellings, longer command names, and incomplete calls remain unchanged.

The transform is idempotent, out-of-place, and shape preserving. It returns Text, propagates undefined state, and rejects defined non-Text Notes. Its scanner is linear in source bytes; recursion follows syntactic nesting depth and does not invoke a TeX engine.

Example 1: Variants, Nesting, And Outer Whitespace¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\dfrac { a + {b} } { \tfrac{ c }{ d } })",
    R"(\cfrac{x}{y} + \frac { 1 } { 2 })"});
std::cout << source.tex().simplify_fractions() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["\\frac{a + {b}}{\\frac{c}{d}}", "\\frac{x}{y} + \\frac{1}{2}"]

Example 2: Near Misses And Malformed Calls Survive¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    R"(\operatorname{x} \fraction{a}{b} \\dfrac{a}{b} \frac{broken})");
std::cout << source.tex().simplify_fractions() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"\\operatorname{x} \\fraction{a}{b} \\\\dfrac{a}{b} \\frac{broken}"

Example 3: Matrix Shape Is Preserved¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(\tfrac{a}{b})", "plain",
                             R"(\dfrac {x}{y})", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << grid.tex().simplify_fractions() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["\\frac{a}{b}", "plain"],
  ["\\frac{x}{y}", ""]
]

Example 4: Idempotence, Undefined State, And Dtype¶

const auto once = pluss::make_note(R"(\dfrac {a}{b})")
                      .tex().simplify_fractions();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "idempotent="
          << ((once == once.tex().simplify_fractions()).all().bool_item())
          << " undefined="
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().simplify_fractions().defined()
          << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex()
      .simplify_fractions();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

idempotent=true undefined=false
Int64: rejected
